original_value: In many Internet of Things (IoT) applications, large numbers of small sensor data are delivered in the network, which may cause heavy traffics. To reduce the number of messages delivered from the sensor devices to the IoT server, a promising approach is to aggregate several small IoT messages into a large packet before they are delivered through the network. When the packets arrive at the destination, they are disaggregated into the original IoT messages. In the existing solutions, packet aggregation/disaggregation is performed by software at the server, which results in long delays and low throughputs. To resolve the above issue, this paper utilizes the programmable Software Defined Networking (SDN) switch to program quick packet aggregation and disaggregation. Specifically, we consider the Programming Protocol-Independent Packet Processor (P4) technology. We design and develop novel P4 programs for aggregation and disaggregation in commercial P4 switches. Our study indicates that packet aggregation can be achieved in a P4 switch with its line rate (without extra packet processing cost). On the other hand, to disaggregate a packet that combines N IoT messages, the processing time is about the same as processing N individual IoT messages. Our implementation conducts IoT message aggregation at the highest bit rate (100 Gbps) that has not been found in the literature. We further propose to provide a small buffer in the P4 switch to significantly reduce the processing power for disaggregating a packet.

result.paraphrase: In many Internet of Things (IoT) deployments, huge volumes of small sensor data flow through the network and can create heavy traffic. A promising way to cut the number of messages sent from sensor devices to the IoT server is to combine multiple small IoT messages into one large packet before transmission. Once the packets reach the destination, they are split back into the original IoT messages. In current solutions, aggregation and disaggregation are handled by software on the server, leading to long delays and low throughput. To address this problem, this paper uses a programmable Software Defined Networking (SDN) switch to implement fast packet aggregation and disaggregation. In particular, we consider Programming Protocol-Independent Packet Processor (P4) technology. We design and develop new P4 programs for aggregation and disaggregation on commercial P4 switches. Our study shows that packet aggregation can be performed in a P4 switch at line rate without additional packet processing cost. For disaggregation, a packet containing N IoT messages takes about the same processing time as N separate IoT messages. Our implementation performs IoT message aggregation at the highest bit rate reported in the literature, 100 Gbps. We also propose adding a small buffer in the P4 switch to greatly reduce the processing power needed to disaggregate a packet.
